The paper is not among the listed permanent documents, so I’m checking the indexed sources first, then I’ll verify the paper’s calculation if needed.



Searching the indexed documents for the paper title and fish-bag volume.
```python
paper_search = await knowledge_search_knowledge("Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish Maintain Dragon Diet fish bag volume", scope="all")
print(paper_search)
```
The indexed-document search did not provide the paper’s calculation, so I’m searching the public web for the University of Leicester paper and its stated bag volume.
```python
paper_web_search = await web_search('"Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragon’s Diet" fish bag volume m3', max_results=5)
print(paper_web_search)
```
The search result is now available; I’m extracting the specific numerical volume from the returned snippets.
```python
print(paper_web_search)
```
I’m running a focused public-web lookup for the paper’s numerical result.
```python
fish_bag_lookup = await web_search('"fish bag" "Hiccup" dragon diet volume', max_results=10)
print(fish_bag_lookup)
```
The initial lookup was too broad; I’m narrowing it to the University of Leicester publication and the calculation’s units.
```python
leicester_lookup = await web_search('"Can Hiccup" "University of Leicester" fish', max_results=10)
print(leicester_lookup)
```
I’m making one final targeted lookup for the exact phrase used in the paper’s volume calculation.
```python
exact_lookup = await web_search('"volume of the bag" fish Hiccup', max_results=10)
print(exact_lookup)
```
I’m checking an external search endpoint directly as a fallback to retrieve the paper text rather than estimate the value.
```python
search_endpoint = await run_command("python -c \"import urllib.parse,urllib.request; u='https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q='+urllib.parse.quote('Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish Maintain Dragon Diet fish bag volume'); print(urllib.request.urlopen(u,timeout=20).read().decode('utf-8','ignore')[:12000])\"")
print(search_endpoint)
```
